results.question: What megohm-meter voltage should be applied when megger-testing the main stator windings of an ABB machine?
results.source: §7.6.4.4, p.91 (source text says 'insulation resistance test', not 'megger'/'megohm-meter')
results.rewritten_query: ABB machine main stator winding insulation-resistance testing: recommended megohmmeter test voltage.
results.answer:
## Required test voltage

Apply **1,000 VDC** when megger-testing the **main stator windings** of an ABB machine. The test duration is **1 minute**, after which record the insulation-resistance value. [3]

The **100 VDC** value applies to other auxiliaries, not the main stator windings; the space-heater test voltage is **500 VDC**. [1]

## Procedure and conditions

1. Confirm that all power-supply cables are disconnected. [3]

2. Ensure that the current-transformer secondary connections, including spare cores, are not open. [3]

3. Earth the machine frame and any stator windings not being tested. [3]

4. Measure the winding temperature. [3]

5. Earth all resistance-temperature detectors. [3]

6. Remove any voltage-transformer earthing, if present. [3]

7. Connect the insulation-resistance meter in the terminal box between the machine frame and the stator winding. [3]

8. For a whole-winding test, keep the three stator phases connected at the neutral point while the machine frame is earthed. [3]

![Figure 39 Connections of the stator windings for insulation resistance measurements](diagrams/41ec3469-76ef-43af-af26-ddc71f09336b/fig39_1.png)

9. If the whole-winding insulation resistance is lower than specified and the phases can be disconnected, measure each phase separately, earthing the frame and the two phases not being tested. [3]

10. After testing, briefly earth the winding phases to discharge them. [3]

The supplied ABB context does not provide a numerical minimum insulation-resistance acceptance limit or specific causes for a low main-stator reading.

[1] ABB Manual for Induction Motors and Generators EN, p. 94 · 7.6.5 Insulation resistance measurement for auxiliaries
To ensure correct operation of the machines protections and other auxiliaries, their condition can be determined by an insulation resistance test. The procedure is described in detail in Chapter 7.6 Maintenance of stator and rotor windings. The test voltage for the space heater should be 500 VDC and for other auxiliaries 100 VDC. The insulation resistance measurement for Pt-100 detectors or proximity probes is not recommended.

[2] Siemens Manual Vertical Induction Motors EN, p. 10 · Insulation Resistance
Check insulation resistance prior to connecting motor to power supply. A hand cranked or solid state electronic insulation resistance tester, at least 500 volts d.c., but not over rated voltage, is usually used (see Maintenance).
See IEEE Recommended Practice for Testing Insulation Resistance Rotating Machinery IEEE Std 43.

[3] ABB Manual for Induction Motors and Generators EN, p. 92 · 7.6.4.4 Stator winding insulation resistance measurement
The insulation resistance is measured using an insulation resistance meter. The test voltage is 1000 VDC. The test time is 1 minute, after which the insulation resistance value is recorded. Before the insulation resistance test is conducted, the following actions must be taken:
- Check that the secondary connections of the current transformers (CT's), including spare cores are not open. See Figure 39 Connections of the stator windings for insulation resistance measurements.
- Verify that all power supply cables are disconnected.
- Verify that the frame of the machine and the stator windings not being tested are earthed.
- The winding temperature is measured.
- All resistance temperature detectors are earthed.
- Possible earthing of voltage transformers (not common) must be removed.
The insulation resistance measuring should be carried out in the terminal box. The test is usually performed to the whole winding as a group, in which case the meter is connected between the frame of the machine and the winding; See Figure 39 Connections of the stator windings for insulation resistance measurements. The frame is earthed and the three phases of the stator winding remain connected at the neutral point, see Figure 39 Connections of the stator windings for insulation resistance measurements.
If the measured insulation resistance of the whole winding is lower than specified, and the phase windings can easily be disconnected from each other, each phase can also be measured separately. This is not possible for all machines. In this measurement, the tester is connected between the frame of the machine and one of the windings. The frame and the two phases not measured are earthed; see Figure 39 Connections of the stator windings for insulation resistance measurements.
Carbon dust on slip rings and naked copper surfaces lower the insulation resistance values of the rotor.
When phases are measured separately, all star-points of the winding system must be removed. If the star-point of the component cannot be removed, as in a typical tri-phase voltage transformer, the whole component must be removed.
Figure 39 Connections of the stator windings for insulation resistance measurements
- a) Insulation resistance measurement for star connected winding.
- b) Insulation resistance measurement for delta connected winding.
- c) Insulation resistance measurement for one phase of the winding. The 'MΩ' represents the insulation resistance meter.
After the insulation resistance measurement the winding phases must be earthed briefly in order to discharge them.
Following chapter for rotor type: Slip rings

Figures for this passage:
- Figure 39 Connections of the stator windings for insulation resistance measurements — image path: diagrams/41ec3469-76ef-43af-af26-ddc71f09336b/fig39_1.png

[4] ABB Manual for Induction Motors and Generators EN, p. 93 · 7.6.4.5 Rotor winding insulation resistance measurement
The insulation resistance of the rotor winding is measured with an insulation resistance meter. The test voltage of the rotor windings should be 1000 VDC. Required notes and measures:
- Verify that all power supply cables are disconnected from the main supply.
- Verify the slip ring unit connection cables are disconnected from their supply.
- Verify that the frame of the machine and the stator windings are earthed.
- The shaft is earthed.
- The rotor winding phases not been tested are earthed. The rotor winding can be internally connected in a delta or star connection. If this is the case, it is not possible to measure the phases individually.
- The carbon brush connections are checked to be in good order.
- The measurement device is checked.
- The stator winding temperatures are measured, and considered as a reference value for the rotor winding temperature.
The insulation resistance meter is connected between the whole rotor winding and the shaft of the machine, see Figure 40 Insulation resistance measurement of the rotor winding. After performed rotor winding measurements, the rotor winding phases must be briefly earthed in order to discharge the windings.
Figure 40 Insulation resistance measurement of the rotor winding
In the figure above the rotor is star-connected.

Figures for this passage:
- Figure 40 Insulation resistance measurement of the rotor winding — image path: diagrams/41ec3469-76ef-43af-af26-ddc71f09336b/fig40_1.png

[5] ABB Manual for Induction Motors and Generators EN, p. 36 · 3.3.1 Insulation resistance measurements
Before a machine is started up for the first time, after a long period of standstill or within the scope of general maintenance work, the insulation resistance of the machine must be measured. This includes measuring the stature winding and all auxiliary devices. For machines equipped with slip ring, the measuring also includes the rotor winding, see Chapter 7.6.4 Insulation resistance test.

results.question: How tightly, in Nm, must an oiled M10 bolt of property class 8.8 be fastened on an ABB machine?
results.source: Table 7, p.79 (source uses 'tightening torque', not 'how tightly fastened')
results.rewritten_query: What is the specified tightening torque in Nm for an oiled M10 property class 8.8 bolt on an ABB electric machine?
results.answer:
## Required tightening torque

For a **standard ABB fastening**, an **oiled M10 bolt of property class 8.8** should be tightened to **44 Nm**. [1]

| Bolt size | Condition | Property class | Tightening torque |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| M10 | Oiled | 8.8 | **44 Nm** [1] |

## Conditions and procedure

1. Confirm that the bolt is an **M10, property class 8.8** fastener and that it is **oiled**. [1]
2. Check that no different tightening value is specified elsewhere in the ABB manual for the particular component. [1]
3. Do not apply the 44 Nm general value to excluded items such as **diodes, support insulators, bearings, cable terminals or pole fastenings, bus bar terminals, surge arrestors, capacitors, current transformers, rectifier and thyristor bridges**, or any item with another specified value. [1]
4. If no exception or component-specific value applies, tighten the bolt to **44 Nm**. [1]

results.question: At what oscillation speed does the alarm trigger for a rigidly mounted ABB bearing housing?
results.rewritten_query: What oscillation velocity triggers the alarm for a rigidly mounted ABB bearing housing?
results.answer:
## Alarm limit

The initial alarm triggers at **3.4 mm/s r.m.s. vibration velocity** for a **rigid-support ABB bearing housing**. [1]

| Support class | Initial ALARM [mm/s r.m.s.] | TRIP [mm/s r.m.s.] |
|---|---:|---:|
| Rigid | 3.4 [1] | 7.1 [1] |
| Flexible | 5.3 [1] | 11.0 [1] |

These are initial, standard values; after the site steady-state baseline is established, the alarm setting should be adjusted accordingly, and the values may be modified when additional information about the machine and application is available. [1]

## Possible causes and checks

An alarm value alone does not identify the cause. For bearing noise or vibration, ABB lists possible causes including: [4]

- Insufficient lubrication or unsuitable grease quality or viscosity. [4]
- Reduced grease quality or incorrect regreasing period. [4]
- Faulty operating conditions. [4]
- Damaged bearing parts, bearing currents, or complete bearing failure. [4]
- Normal bearing wear. [4]
- Faulty bearing seals or incorrect bearing assembly. [4]
- Deformed roller elements or foreign matter inside the bearing. [4]

## Recommended procedure

1. Confirm that the measured quantity is bearing-housing vibration velocity in **mm/s r.m.s.** and compare it with the **3.4 mm/s r.m.s.** initial alarm value. [1]
2. Compare the reading with the machine’s established steady-state baseline, since ABB recommends adjusting the alarm setting after that baseline has been established. [1]
3. Monitor the driving–driven machine system and investigate the bearing, lubrication, seals, assembly, operating conditions, and alignment if vibration is elevated. [3][4]
4. Treat **7.1 mm/s r.m.s.** as the initial rigid-support trip value, subject to the same qualification that these standard values can be adjusted when additional machine and application information is available. [1]

results.question: What is the exact re-greasing interval, in hours, for the rolling bearings of an ABB machine?
results.expected_answer: No universal number — the interval is found on the bearing plate (machine-specific); regardless, re-greasing must occur at least once per year, and the interval halves per 15°C rise above the 70°C baseline
results.rewritten_query: ABB machine rolling-bearing re-greasing interval in operating hours.
results.answer:
## Answer

The exact re-greasing interval in hours cannot be determined from the provided context.

The interval is specified on the machine’s bearing plate; no bearing-plate value is provided here. [1][4] The re-greasing interval must not exceed 12 months, and the bearings must be re-greased at least once per year. [1][5]

The interval values are based on a bearing operating temperature of **70 °C (160 °F)**. [1]

- For every **15 °C (30 °F) increase** in bearing temperature, the interval should be **halved**. [1]
- For every **15 °C (30 °F) decrease**, the interval may be **doubled**. [1]
- Higher bearing operating temperature shortens the interval. [1]

### Re-greasing procedure while running

1. Verify that the grease is suitable. [2]
2. Clean the grease nipples and the surrounding area. [2]
3. Verify that the lubrication channel is open; open its handle if fitted. [2]
4. Press the specified amount and type of grease into the bearing. [2]
5. Allow the machine to run for **1–2 hours** so excess grease is forced out; bearing temperature may temporarily increase. [2]
6. Close the handle if fitted. [2]

[1] ABB Manual for Induction Motors and Generators EN, p. 85 · 7.5.3.3 Re-greasing intervals
Rolling bearings of electrical machines need to be re-greased at regular intervals. The re-greasing interval is found on the bearing plate.
NOTE:
Regardless of the re-greasing interval, the bearings need to be re-greased at least once per year.
The re-greasing intervals are calculated for an operating temperature of 70°C (160°F). If the operating temperature is lower or higher than the assumed, the re-grease interval has to be altered accordingly. Higher operating temperature decreases the re-greasing interval.
NOTE:
An increase in the ambient temperature raises the temperature of the bearings correspondingly. The values for the re-greasing interval should be halved for every 15°C (30°F) increase in bearing temperature and may be once doubled for a 15°C (30°F) decrease in bearing temperature.

[2] ABB Manual for Induction Motors and Generators EN, p. 85 · Manual re-greasing while the machine is running
Re-greasing while the machine is running:
- Verify that the grease to be used is suitable.
- Clean the grease nipples and the area around them.
- Verify that the lubrication channel is open, if equipped with a handle, open it.
- Press the specified amount and type of grease into the bearing.
- Let the machine run 1-2 hours in order to ensure that all excess grease is forced out of the bearing. The bearing temperature may temporarily increase during this time.
- If equipped with a handle, close it.
NOTE:
Beware of all rotating parts during the re-greasing.

[3] ABB Manual for Induction Motors and Generators EN, p. 84 · 7.5.2.5 Oil change schedule for mineral oils
For self-lubricated bearings cleaning intervals with oil changes of approximately 8000 operating hours are recommended and approx. 20000 operating hours for bearings with oil circulation systems.
Shorter oil change intervals may be necessary in case of frequent start-ups, high oil temperatures or excessively high contamination due to external influences.
The correct oil change interval can be found on the bearing plate and dimensional drawing, see Chapter 2.1.2 Bearing plate.
Following chapter for bearing type: Rolling bearing

[4] ABB Manual for Induction Motors and Generators EN, p. 85 · 7.5.3.4 Re-greasing
All rolling bearings of rotating electrical machines need to be re-greased, see Chapter 7.5.3.3 Re-greasing intervals. The re-greasing can be performed either manually or by means of an automatic system. In either case, it has to be verified that a suitable amount of the correct grease is entering the bearing at suitable intervals.
NOTE:
Grease can cause skin irritation and eye inflammation. Follow all safety precautions specified by the grease manufacturer.

[5] ABB Manual for Induction Motors and Generators EN, p. 66 · Figure 32 Example of lubrication channel through bearing arrangement of horizontal machine
NOTE:
NOTE:
Start-up greasing may take several grease portions (3-10 times amount mentioned at the lubrication plate).
The re-lubrication interval will never be longer than 12 months.
The type of original grease used is found on the bearing plate on the machine. Acceptable types of grease can be found in Chapter 7.5.3 Rolling bearings.
NOTE:
Do not mix greases! There must be only one type of grease inside the bearing - not mixture of two or more greases.
The temperature of the bearings will initially increase because of the excess grease. After few hours, the excess grease will be discharged through the lubrication valve and the temperature of the bearing will return to normal running temperature.
If available, and after the machine has been running for several hours, measure the vibrations or SPM-values from the SPM-nipples, and record the values for future reference use.

results.question: What is the recommended bearing regreasing interval for a Siemens 1LA8 motor?
results.rewritten_query: Recommended bearing regreasing interval for a Siemens 1LA8 electric motor.
results.answer:
## Direct answer

The context does not provide a numeric regreasing interval specifically for a Siemens 1LA8 motor. For this motor, use the interval and grease type stated on the motor’s lubrication plate; the Siemens manual identifies that plate as the source for both values.[3]

## Required checks

1. Locate the motor lubrication plate and record its specified regreasing interval and recommended grease type.[3]
2. For a newly installed motor, check that the bearings have been properly lubricated.[3]
3. Do not assume that the ABB interval values apply as the Siemens 1LA8’s model-specific interval; the supplied Siemens passage does not state a numeric value.

## Relevant general limits

The ABB guidance states that bearings must be regreased at least once per year, regardless of the stated interval.[1]

ABB’s interval calculations assume a bearing operating temperature of 70°C (160°F); higher bearing temperature shortens the interval.[1]

- For every 15°C (30°F) increase in bearing temperature, the interval should be halved.[1]
- For every 15°C (30°F) decrease in bearing temperature, the interval may be doubled.[1]

If grease specifications are required, the ABB guidance gives the following properties:

| Property | Requirement |
|---|---|
| Grease type | Special rolling-bearing grease.[2] |
| Base soap and oil | Lithium-complex soap with mineral or PAO oil.[2] |
| Base-oil viscosity | 100–160 cSt at 40°C (105°F).[2] |
| Consistency | NLGI grade 1.5–3; NLGI grade 2 or 3 is recommended for vertically mounted or hot-condition machines.[2] |
| Continuous temperature range | −30°C (−20°F) to at least +120°C (250°F).[2] |

Do not mix greases; only one grease type should be present inside the bearing.[2]

[1] ABB Manual for Induction Motors and Generators EN, p. 85 · 7.5.3.3 Re-greasing intervals
Rolling bearings of electrical machines need to be re-greased at regular intervals. The re-greasing interval is found on the bearing plate.
NOTE:
Regardless of the re-greasing interval, the bearings need to be re-greased at least once per year.
The re-greasing intervals are calculated for an operating temperature of 70°C (160°F). If the operating temperature is lower or higher than the assumed, the re-grease interval has to be altered accordingly. Higher operating temperature decreases the re-greasing interval.
NOTE:
An increase in the ambient temperature raises the temperature of the bearings correspondingly. The values for the re-greasing interval should be halved for every 15°C (30°F) increase in bearing temperature and may be once doubled for a 15°C (30°F) decrease in bearing temperature.

[2] ABB Manual for Induction Motors and Generators EN, p. 86 · 7.5.3.5 Bearing grease (table)
It is essential to use grease of good quality and with the correct base soap. This will ensure a long and trouble free lifetime of the bearings.
Grease used for re-greasing should have the following properties:
- Be special rolling bearing grease.
- Be of good quality with a lithium complex soap, and with mineral-, or PAO-oil.
- Have a base oil viscosity of 100 to 160 cSt at 40°C (105°F).
- Have a consistency NLGI grade between 1.5 and 3. For vertically or in hot conditions mounted machines, NLGI grade 2 or 3 is recommended.
- Have a continuous temperature range between -30°C (-20°F) and at least +120°C (250°F).
Grease with the correct properties is available from all major lubricant manufacturers. If the make of grease is changed and compatibility is uncertain, consult the manufacturing ABB factory, see Chapter 9.1.3 Contact information for Motors and Generators Service.
| NOTE: | Do not mix greases! There must be only one type of grease inside the bearing - not a mixture of two or more greases. |
| - | - |
| NOTE: | Grease additives are recommended. However, a written guarantee should be obtained from the lubricant manufacturer stating that the additives do not damage the bearings or the properties of the grease in the field of the operating temperature. This is especially important for EP additives. |
| NOTE: | Lubricants containing EP admixtures are not recommended. |

[3] Siemens Manual Vertical Induction Motors EN, p. 19 · Bearing Lubricants - Grease
Prior to shipment, bearings are lubricated with the proper amount and grade of grease to provide satisfactory service under normal operation and conditions. See the lubrication plate mounted on the motor for regreasing intervals and recommended type of grease. It is good practice, however, to check bearings of newly installed machines for proper lubrication.

[4] ABB Manual for Induction Motors and Generators EN, p. 84 · 7.5.2.5 Oil change schedule for mineral oils
For self-lubricated bearings cleaning intervals with oil changes of approximately 8000 operating hours are recommended and approx. 20000 operating hours for bearings with oil circulation systems.
Shorter oil change intervals may be necessary in case of frequent start-ups, high oil temperatures or excessively high contamination due to external influences.
The correct oil change interval can be found on the bearing plate and dimensional drawing, see Chapter 2.1.2 Bearing plate.
Following chapter for bearing type: Rolling bearing

[5] ABB Manual for Induction Motors and Generators EN, p. 85 · 7.5.3.4 Re-greasing
All rolling bearings of rotating electrical machines need to be re-greased, see Chapter 7.5.3.3 Re-greasing intervals. The re-greasing can be performed either manually or by means of an automatic system. In either case, it has to be verified that a suitable amount of the correct grease is entering the bearing at suitable intervals.
NOTE:
Grease can cause skin irritation and eye inflammation. Follow all safety precautions specified by the grease manufacturer.

results.question: What one-minute insulation resistance should a Siemens vertical motor with MICLAD VPI insulation exceed?
results.expected_answer: Greater than 1000 megohms after one minute (values above 5000 megohms are common)
results.rewritten_query: Minimum acceptable one-minute insulation resistance for a Siemens vertical motor with MICLAD VPI insulation.
results.answer:
## Required value

A Siemens vertical motor with MICLAD™ VPI insulation should have an insulation resistance **greater than 1000 MΩ after one minute**. Values above **5000 MΩ** are common. **[1]**

## Test conditions and procedure

1. Check the insulation resistance before connecting the motor to the power supply. **[2]**
2. Use a hand-cranked or solid-state insulation-resistance tester applying **at least 500 V**, but **not more than the motor’s rated voltage**. **[1][2]**
3. Apply the test voltage for one minute and record the insulation-resistance value. **[1]**
4. If the value is low, investigate excess humidity or dirt, which can reduce insulation resistance even when the insulation itself remains intact. **[3]**
5. If cleaning is performed, measure the stator winding insulation resistance both before and after cleaning. **[4]**

contexts:
[1] Siemens Manual Vertical Induction Motors EN, p. 18 · Insulation Resistance
Check insulation resistance periodically. Use a hand cranked or solid state insulation resistance tester and test with at least 500 volts, but not greater than motor rated voltage.
For motors with newer insulation systems such as MICLAD™ VPI, the insulation resistance after one minute should be greater than 1000 megohms. (Values in excess of 5000 megohms are common.) For older motors, the minimum value recommended in IEEE Standard 43 can be used. The value in megohms, when corrected to 40°C, is equal to the motor rated voltage in kilovolts plus 1. For example, for a motor with a rated voltage of 2300 volts, the limit value would be:
2.3 + 1 = 3.3 (megohms).

[2] Siemens Manual Vertical Induction Motors EN, p. 10 · Insulation Resistance
Check insulation resistance prior to connecting motor to power supply. A hand cranked or solid state electronic insulation resistance tester, at least 500 volts d.c., but not over rated voltage, is usually used (see Maintenance).
See IEEE Recommended Practice for Testing Insulation Resistance Rotating Machinery IEEE Std 43.

[3] ABB Manual for Induction Motors and Generators EN, p. 92 · 7.6.4.3 Minimum values for insulation resistance
Criteria for windings in a normal condition:
Generally, the insulation resistance values for dry windings should exceed the minimum values significantly. Definite values are impossible to give, because resistance varies depending on the machine type and local conditions. In addition, the insulation resistance is affected by the age and usage of the machine. Therefore, the following values can only be considered as guidelines.
The insulation resistance limits, which are given below, are valid at 40 °C, and when the test voltage has been applied for 1 minute or longer.
- Rotor.
For induction machines with wound rotors: R(1-10 min at 40 °C) > 5 MΩ.
NOTE:
- Stator.
For new stators: R(1-10 min at 40 °C) > 1000 MΩ. If the measuring conditions are extremely warm and humid, R(1-10 min at 40 °C) values above 100 MΩ can be accepted.
For used stators: R(1-10 min at 40 °C) > 100 MΩ.
NOTE:
If the values given here are not reached, the reason for the low insulation resistance should be determined. A low insulation resistance value is often caused by excess humidity or dirt, although the actual insulation is intact.

[4] Siemens Manual Vertical Induction Motors EN, p. 18 · Stator Cleaning
MICLAD™ form wound VPI (vacuum pressure impregnated) insulated coils may be cleaned with a quick drying solvent and lint free cloths or steam cleaned with low-pressure steam, then the entire stator oven baked at 200°F for 12 hours and then 230°F for 12 hours.
The stator winding insulation resistance should be measured before and after any cleaning operation.
The windings may be cleaned with a solvent compatible with the insulation system and oven dried. Water and detergents with an oven drying cycle may be used as an alternate on MICLAD™ VPI insulation systems.
MICLAD™ is a Siemens trademark.

[5] ABB Manual for Induction Motors and Generators EN, p. 92 · 7.6.4.4 Stator winding insulation resistance measurement
The insulation resistance is measured using an insulation resistance meter. The test voltage is 1000 VDC. The test time is 1 minute, after which the insulation resistance value is recorded. Before the insulation resistance test is conducted, the following actions must be taken:
- Check that the secondary connections of the current transformers (CT's), including spare cores are not open. See Figure 39 Connections of the stator windings for insulation resistance measurements.
- Verify that all power supply cables are disconnected.
- Verify that the frame of the machine and the stator windings not being tested are earthed.
- The winding temperature is measured.
- All resistance temperature detectors are earthed.
- Possible earthing of voltage transformers (not common) must be removed.
The insulation resistance measuring should be carried out in the terminal box. The test is usually performed to the whole winding as a group, in which case the meter is connected between the frame of the machine and the winding; See Figure 39 Connections of the stator windings for insulation resistance measurements. The frame is earthed and the three phases of the stator winding remain connected at the neutral point, see Figure 39 Connections of the stator windings for insulation resistance measurements.
If the measured insulation resistance of the whole winding is lower than specified, and the phase windings can easily be disconnected from each other, each phase can also be measured separately. This is not possible for all machines. In this measurement, the tester is connected between the frame of the machine and one of the windings. The frame and the two phases not measured are earthed; see Figure 39 Connections of the stator windings for insulation resistance measurements.
Carbon dust on slip rings and naked copper surfaces lower the insulation resistance values of the rotor.
When phases are measured separately, all star-points of the winding system must be removed. If the star-point of the component cannot be removed, as in a typical tri-phase voltage transformer, the whole component must be removed.
Figure 39 Connections of the stator windings for insulation resistance measurements
- a) Insulation resistance measurement for star connected winding.
- b) Insulation resistance measurement for delta connected winding.
- c) Insulation resistance measurement for one phase of the winding. The 'MΩ' represents the insulation resistance meter.
After the insulation resistance measurement the winding phases must be earthed briefly in order to discharge them.

results.question: How should a Toshiba TM21 motor be prepared for long-term storage?
results.rewritten_query: Toshiba TM21 motor long-term storage preparation procedures.
results.answer:
## Direct answer

The provided context does not contain Toshiba TM21-specific storage instructions. Based on the available manufacturer guidance, prepare the motor for long-term storage as follows.

## Storage procedure

1. Store the motor in a clean, dry, well-ventilated location that is free from vibration and rapid or wide temperature variations. [4]

2. Treat the motor as being in storage when installation or operation is delayed for more than 30 days, when there are operating-cycle intervals of 30 days, or when the plant or department is shut down for 30 days. [4]

3. If supplied, energize the motor’s space heaters during storage. [4]

4. Rotate the shaft by hand at least 10 complete turns once each month to distribute lubricant over the bearings, retard oxidation or corrosion, and help prevent false brinelling. [4]

5. If the enclosed motor has drain plugs, remove them periodically during storage to drain accumulated water. [4]

6. If the motor has been out of service or in storage for more than 30 days, consult the applicable storage recommendations before returning it to service. [1]

## Before returning the motor to service

1. Relubricate the bearings in accordance with the motor’s bearing instructions. [2]

2. Remove desiccant, if present. [2]

3. Test the insulation resistance of the windings before placing the motor in service. [2]

4. Perform an external inspection to confirm that the motor is clean, ventilation openings are unobstructed, and no damage has occurred. [3]

5. Rotate the shaft to check for bearing roughness and interference between rotating and stationary parts. [3]

6. Perform a bench test for excessive current draw, noise, or vibration. [3]

Question: After storing my motor for an extended period of time, I am now ready to install it. Is there any specific inspection procedure that must be followed?
Answer: Yes. Following storage, an extensive inspection must be performed on a motor by one of our authorized service stations. This inspection must include the following elements:
- 1) Render an external inspection of the motor to assure the unit is clean, ventilation openings are free of obstructions, and no damage has occurred.
- 2) Perform a megger test of motor windings to insure satisfactory insulation resistance.
- 3) Rotate the shaft to check for roughness in bearings or interference between rotating and stationary parts.
- 4) Perform a bench test on the unit to check for excessive amp. draw, noise, or vibration.
- 5) Regrease the motor bearings (as applicable) in accordance with the unit's operating instruction folder.
- 6) The authorized service station must install a plate/tag indicating the date of inspection. Make any corrections which inspection shows to be needed.

[4] Siemens Manual Vertical Induction Motors EN, p. 5 · Temporary Storage
If the equipment is not to be installed and operated soon after arrival, store it in a clean, dry, well- ventilated place, free from vibration and rapid or wide variations in temperature. Rotate the shaft a minimum of 10 complete turns by hand each month to coat the bearings with lubricant which will retard oxidation or corrosion, and prevent possible false brinelling. If drain plugs are provided in enclosed motors, they must be removed periodically to drain any water accumulation from the motor. Consider a unit in storage when:
1. It has been delivered to the job site and is awaiting installation.
2. It has been installed but operation is delayed over 30 days pending completion of plant construction.
3. There are long (30 day) periods between operating cycles.
4. The plant (or department) is shut down for 30 days.
5. Energize space heaters, if supplied.

Motors are designed to give many years of reliable service with a minimum of attention. Trouble-free operation cannot be expected if proper maintenance is postponed or neglected.

results.question: What vibration alarm limit does GE Vernova specify for its vertical induction motors?
results.rewritten_query: GE Vernova vertical induction motor vibration alarm limit specifications.
results.answer:
## Answer

The provided context does **not specify a vibration alarm limit for GE Vernova vertical induction motors**.

The closest applicable data in the context is for **Siemens vertical induction motors**, and it should not be treated as a GE Vernova specification:

| Measurement | 3600 RPM | 1800 RPM | 1200 RPM | 900 RPM and slower |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Shaft vibration alarm, mils peak-to-peak | 2.8 | 3.2 | 3.8 | 4.5 |
| Shaft vibration trip, mils peak-to-peak | 3.3 | 3.7 | 4.3 | 5.0 |
| Housing vibration trip, in./sec. | 0.25 | 0.25 | 0.25 | 0.25 |

[3]

The context does not provide a GE Vernova alarm value, nor does it identify the Siemens values as applicable to GE Vernova motors.

For the documented Siemens procedure when vibration is excessive:

1. Tighten the flange mounting bolts, check end play, run the motor at minimum load, and check vibration. [2]
2. Loosen the flange mounting bolts and shift the motor within the mounting-flange clearance to reduce vibration. [2]
3. If vibration remains excessive, check shaft alignment and system reed frequency when the motor is coupled to a load. [2]

results.question: What is the NEMA MG1 unfiltered vibration limit for a resiliently mounted Siemens vertical motor running at 900 RPM?
results.rewritten_query: NEMA MG 1 unfiltered vibration limit, including allowable value and units, for a resiliently mounted Siemens vertical motor operating at 900 RPM.
results.answer:
## Limit

The NEMA MG1 unfiltered vibration limit is **0.12 in/s peak (3.0 mm/s)** at 900 RPM for a resiliently mounted Siemens vertical motor. [1]

| Speed, RPM | Rotational frequency, Hz | Unfiltered velocity limit, in/s peak (mm/s) |
|---:|---:|---:|
| 900 | 15 | 0.12 (3.0) [1] |

## Check procedure

1. Tighten the flange mounting bolts and check end play. [1]
2. Run the motor at minimum load and measure vibration. [1]
3. If vibration exceeds **0.12 in/s peak (3.0 mm/s)**, loosen the flange mounting bolts and shift the motor within the mounting-flange clearance. [1]
4. If shifting does not reduce vibration to the acceptable limit and the motor is coupled to a load, check shaft alignment and system reed frequency. [1]

When the machine shaft is rotating, a permanent magnet synchronous machine induces voltage to the terminals. [3] Siemens Manual Vertical Induction Motors EN, p. 16 · Maintenance Checklist
1. Verify motor is clean and verify that stator and rotor ventilation passages are unobstructed.
2. Check for excessive loading or service factor.
3. Verify winding temperature rise not in excess of rated value.
4. Verify insulation resistance is above recommended minimum.
5. Verify voltage and frequency variation.
6. Check air gap.
7. Verify that bearing temperatures are within limits and that lubricant is clean and proper level maintained.
8. Verify no unusual vibration or noise exists.
9. Check alignment.
10. Check for proper lubrication.
A definite schedule of preventive maintenance inspections should be established to avoid breakdown, serious damage and extensive downtime. The schedule will depend on operating conditions and experience with similar equipment. To assure adequate maintenance, and warranty consideration, it is essential that complete records be kept for each motor including description and rating, maintenance schedule and repairs required or carried out.
This checklist does not represent an exhaustive survey of maintenance steps necessary to ensure safe operation of this equipment. Particular applications may require further procedures. Should further information be desired or should particular problems arise which are not covered sufficiently for the purchaser's purposes, the matter should be referred to the local Siemens Sales Office.
Improper maintenance can cause death, serious injury or property damage.
Use only factory authorized parts for repair of equipment. Maintenance should be performed only by qualified personnel.

[4] ABB Manual for Induction Motors and Generators EN, p. 49 · 3.7 Care after installation
If the machine will not be in operation for a longer period after it has been installed, the same measures as mentioned above in Chapter 2.6.1 Short term storage (less than 2 months) should be applied. Remember to rotate the shaft 10 revolutions at least every 3 months, and that self-lubricated bearings must be filled with oil. If external vibration is present, the shaft coupling should be opened and suitable rubber blocks should be placed under the feet of the machine.

[5] ABB Manual for Induction Motors and Generators EN, p. 3 · 4. Installation
Take care of even support, solid foot or flange mounting, and exact alignment. Avoid resonances with rotational frequency and double mains frequency as a result of assembly. Turn rotor and listen for abnormal slip noises. Check direction of rotation in uncoupled state.
Follow the manufacturer's instructions when mounting or removing couplings or other drive elements and cover them with a touch guard. For trial run in uncoupled state, lock or remove the shaft end key. Avoid excessive radial and axial bearing loads (note manufacturer's documentation). The balance of the machine is indicated as H = Half and F = Full key. In half key cases coupling must be half key balanced. In full key cases coupling must be balanced without a key. In case of protruding, visible part of the shaft end key, establish mechanical balance.
Make necessary ventilation and cooling system connections. The ventilation must not be obstructed and the exhaust air, also of neighbouring sets, not taken in directly.

results.question: Using the Siemens winding-resistance method, what is the hot winding temperature if the cold resistance is 0.50 Ω at 25°C and the hot resistance is 0.61 Ω?
results.rewritten_query: Calculate the hot winding temperature using the Siemens winding-resistance method for a cold winding resistance of 0.50 Ω at 25°C and a hot winding resistance of 0.61 Ω, using the copper temperature constant specified in the manual.
results.answer:
## Result

The hot winding temperature cannot be determined reliably from the supplied context because the Siemens temperature equation and the example’s calculated result are missing. The given values are $r=0.50\ \Omega$ at $t=25^\circ\mathrm{C}$ and $R=0.61\ \Omega$, giving a resistance ratio of $R/r=1.22$, but the conversion equation is required to calculate $T$. [2]

## Required procedure

1. Measure the cold resistance after the motor has been idle, preferably before starting, and measure the actual coil temperature rather than assuming it equals the surrounding air temperature. [2]

2. Measure the hot resistance at the motor load terminals immediately after de-energizing the motor and after it has stopped rotating. [2]

3. Use the Siemens winding-resistance equation, with $T$ as hot winding temperature, $R$ as hot resistance, $r$ as cold resistance, and $t$ as cold coil temperature. [2]

4. Use accurate instruments and preferably the same instruments for both hot and cold measurements. [1]

Criteria for windings in a normal condition:
Generally, the insulation resistance values for dry windings should exceed the minimum values significantly. Definite values are impossible to give, because resistance varies depending on the machine type and local conditions. In addition, the insulation resistance is affected by the age and usage of the machine. Therefore, the following values can only be considered as guidelines.
The insulation resistance limits, which are given below, are valid at 40 °C, and when the test voltage has been applied for 1 minute or longer.
- Rotor.

If the values given here are not reached, the reason for the low insulation resistance should be determined. A low insulation resistance value is often caused by excess humidity or dirt, although the actual insulation is intact.

results.rewritten_query: Minimum insulation resistance recommended by Siemens for an older 2,300 V vertical electric motor.
results.answer:
## Minimum value

For an older Siemens vertical motor rated **2300 V**, the minimum insulation resistance is **3.3 MΩ, corrected to 40°C**. [1]

$$
2.3\ \text{kV} + 1 = 3.3\ \text{M}\Omega
$$

## Test conditions and procedure

1. Test the insulation resistance before connecting the motor to the power supply. [2]
2. Use a hand-cranked or solid-state insulation-resistance tester with a test voltage of **at least 500 V**, but **not greater than the motor’s rated voltage**. [1][2]
3. Correct the measured resistance to **40°C** before comparing it with the **3.3 MΩ** minimum. [1]
4. If the value is low, investigate humidity, dirt, or other unsuitable storage or operating conditions; low resistance is often caused by excess humidity or dirt even when the insulation itself remains intact. [3][5]
5. Briefly earth the windings after the measurement to reduce electric-shock risk. [5]

The Siemens passage does not state a separate test duration for the older-motor limit; it specifies that the value must be corrected to 40°C.

[1] Siemens Manual Vertical Induction Motors EN, p. 18 · Insulation Resistance
Check insulation resistance periodically. Use a hand cranked or solid state insulation resistance tester and test with at least 500 volts, but not greater than motor rated voltage.
For motors with newer insulation systems such as MICLAD™ VPI, the insulation resistance after one minute should be greater than 1000 megohms. (Values in excess of 5000 megohms are common.) For older motors, the minimum value recommended in IEEE Standard 43 can be used. The value in megohms, when corrected to 40°C, is equal to the motor rated voltage in kilovolts plus 1. For example, for a motor with a rated voltage of 2300 volts, the limit value would be:
2.3 + 1 = 3.3 (megohms).

[2] Siemens Manual Vertical Induction Motors EN, p. 10 · Insulation Resistance
Check insulation resistance prior to connecting motor to power supply. A hand cranked or solid state electronic insulation resistance tester, at least 500 volts d.c., but not over rated voltage, is usually used (see Maintenance).
See IEEE Recommended Practice for Testing Insulation Resistance Rotating Machinery IEEE Std 43.

[3] ABB Manual for Induction Motors and Generators EN, p. 92 · 7.6.4.3 Minimum values for insulation resistance
Criteria for windings in a normal condition:
Generally, the insulation resistance values for dry windings should exceed the minimum values significantly. Definite values are impossible to give, because resistance varies depending on the machine type and local conditions. In addition, the insulation resistance is affected by the age and usage of the machine. Therefore, the following values can only be considered as guidelines.
The insulation resistance limits, which are given below, are valid at 40 °C, and when the test voltage has been applied for 1 minute or longer.
- Rotor.
For induction machines with wound rotors: R(1-10 min at 40 °C) > 5 MΩ.
NOTE:
- Stator.
For new stators: R(1-10 min at 40 °C) > 1000 MΩ. If the measuring conditions are extremely warm and humid, R(1-10 min at 40 °C) values above 100 MΩ can be accepted.
For used stators: R(1-10 min at 40 °C) > 100 MΩ.
NOTE:
If the values given here are not reached, the reason for the low insulation resistance should be determined. A low insulation resistance value is often caused by excess humidity or dirt, although the actual insulation is intact.

[4] ABB Manual for Induction Motors and Generators EN, p. 94 · 7.6.5 Insulation resistance measurement for auxiliaries
To ensure correct operation of the machines protections and other auxiliaries, their condition can be determined by an insulation resistance test. The procedure is described in detail in Chapter 7.6 Maintenance of stator and rotor windings. The test voltage for the space heater should be 500 VDC and for other auxiliaries 100 VDC. The insulation resistance measurement for Pt-100 detectors or proximity probes is not recommended.

[5] ABB Manual for Induction Motors and Generators EN, p. 90 · 7.6.4 Insulation resistance test
During general maintenance work and before the machine is started up for the first time or after a long period of standstill, the insulation resistance of stator and rotor windings must be measured.
The insulation resistance measurement provides information about the humidity and dirtiness of the insulation. Based upon this information, correct cleaning and drying actions can be determined.
For new machines with dry windings, the insulation resistance is very high. The resistance can, however, be extremely low if the machine has been subjected to incorrect transportation and storage conditions and humidity, or if the machine is operated incorrectly.
NOTE:
Windings should be earthed briefly immediately after measurement in order to avoid risk of electric shock.

results.rewritten_query: Factory-preset end play for a Kingsbury-type thrust bearing.
results.answer: The Kingsbury-type thrust bearing has a factory-preset end play of **0.012–0.017 inches**, established by shims between the thrust plate and the upper guide (upthrust) bearing. [2]

3. NEMA Frame Verticals with Thrust Bearing in Lower Housing

contexts:
[1] Siemens Manual Vertical Induction Motors EN, p. 23 · Lower Guide Bearing
The function of the lower guide bearing with a Kingsbury-type bearing is to provide radial location of the shaft with no thrust or end play limit. This bearing may be one of three types - grease-lubricated ball bearing, oil-lubricated ball bearing, or oil-lubricated sleeve bearing (See Figures 9, 10 and 11).

[2] Siemens Manual Vertical Induction Motors EN, p. 23 · Thrust Bearing
Principle elements of the Kingsbury-type thrust bearing are the rotating thrust runner and the stationary pivotal thrust shoes (See Figure 7) The runner is the highly polished bottom surface of the thrust block and receives the thrust load through a massive nut above the thrust block threaded on the top end of the shaft. The pivotal thrust shoes are faced with tin-hard Babbitt and machined to form an accurate surface plate.
During operation, the thrust bearing revolves in an oil bath which covers the bearing. Each shoe is free to tilt slightly in any direction and sets itself by pivoting at a minute angle causing a wedge-shaped film of oil to form between the shoe and the runner. An end play of 0.012 - 0.017 inches is preset at the factory by shims between the thrust plate and the upper guide (upthrust) bearing.

[3] Siemens Manual Vertical Induction Motors EN, p. 22 · End Play
Machines designed for applications involving primarily continuous heavy downthrust but having momentary upthrust are equipped with angular contact or spherical roller bearings. Spherical roller bearings may be preloaded with springs (See Figure 8). The end play is most often 0.005 to 0.008 in. but see the motor outline for the exact value for your motor. The bottom bearing takes the momentary upthrust and prevents reverse loading of the top bearings. End play is limited by shims when the thrust block is shrunk on the shaft or by tightening the locknut on the shaft above the bearing mounting sleeve. The thrust bearings on 2 pole motors are mounted directly on the shaft and do not require an adjustment by the shims or locknut.

[4] Nidec Motor Manual, p. 24 · I. Spherical Roller Thrust Bearings and Angular Contact Bearings (With Springs)
On spherical roller or angular contact thrust bearings with springs, setting the correct end play for preload requires a controlled assembly method, due to various deflections internal to the motor and friction of locknut threads from spring force. An end play setting of .005 to .008 inches is required to allow the lower guide bearing to return to an unload position when external thrust is applied to the motor (see Figure 5). End play can be properly adjusted by the following recommended procedure:
- A. Place spring retainer, without springs and lower thrust washer of bearing, into upper bracket bearing bore.
- B. Using a depth micrometer, measure the distance between the top of the lower thrust washer and the faced surface on top of the bearing housing. Record this dimension to three decimal places.
- C. Add .005 and .008 inches to the recorded dimension to obtain the correct minimum and maximum settings range for the unit.
- D. Reassemble bearing with springs; motor is now ready to set end play.
NOTE: Certain motor builds require removal of the fabricated steel or cast aluminum oil baffle to provide access for depth micrometer measurements.
Motors built with spherical roller thrust or angular contact bearings with springs require a minimum external thrust load, sufficient to compress upper die springs and unload lower guide bearing from axial spring thrust. Refer to the motor's spring thrust plate for required minimum thrust.
NOTE: Do not run motor without load for more than fifteen minutes, as lower bearing damage may occur and improper seating of thrust bearing may cause vibration.

[5] Siemens Manual Vertical Induction Motors EN, p. 35 · Vertical Solid & Hollow Shaft Nomenclature
Angular Contact Bearing - An antifriction thrust bearing capable of taking high thrust in one axial direction only.
DT Bearing - Two (2) angular contact bearings mounted together to take extra high thrust in one axial direction only.
DB Bearings - Two (2) angular contact bearings mounted together such that each one will take high thrust in opposite directions.
End Play - The axial movement of the shaft.
Four Point Bearing - An angular contact bearing which will take thrust in both directions.
Guide Bearing - The bearing mounted in the housing opposite the thrust bearing. Most are deep groove antifriction bearings.
Thrust block or Bearing Mounting Sleeve - The member keyed to the motor shaft on which the inner race of the thrust bearing is mounted.
Continuous Down Thrust - The thrust developed by the weight of the pump shaft and hydraulic unbalance. This is the thrust value to which the motor thrust bearings are sized.
Maximum Down Thrust - the momentary down thrust that can be developed during shut down of the pump.
Momentary Upthrust - This thrust may develop in some shallow settings during startup. Momentary upthrust is mostly carried by the Guide Bearing in most vertical motors.
Non-Reverse Ratchet or Backstop - A device that permits motor to turn in only one direction. It is used mostly in conjunction with Rigid Couplings to prevent turbine pump backspin caused by the water column receding when the motor is de-energized.

results.question: For a hollow shaft Siemens motor, what dial indicator reading is the limit for acceptable alignment?
results.expected_answer: Readings must not exceed 0.0005 inches at 90-degree increments
results.rewritten_query: Siemens hollow-shaft motor: maximum acceptable dial indicator reading for shaft alignment.
results.answer:
## Acceptable limit

For a hollow-shaft Siemens motor, acceptable alignment occurs when the dial-indicator readings do not exceed **0.0005 inches**. [2]

## Procedure

1. Clamp the dial indicator to the pump shaft, align it with the basebolt plane, and set the indicator to zero. [2]

   ![Figure 2](diagrams/a03aca4e-dbdc-4868-a843-4c240457390e/fig2_1.png)

2. Remove the top cover and rotate both the motor and pump shafts. [2]

3. Record the dial-indicator reading at 90-degree increments from the starting point. [2]

4. If the readings exceed **0.0005 inches**, shim the flange faces as necessary. [2]

5. After alignment and vibration are within limits, engage the drive, run at minimum load, and progressively increase the load while checking vibration until full load is reached. [2]

The provided context does not specify the likely mechanical causes of an alignment reading above the limit.

[1] Siemens Manual Vertical Induction Motors EN, p. 28 · Shaft Runout
The shaft runout is measured with the indicator stationary with respect to the machine and with its point at the end of the finished surface of the shaft. See Figure 13 for typical fixture.
Read the maximum and minimum values on the indicator as the shaft is rotated slowly through 360 degrees. The difference between the readings shall not exceed 0.003 inches.

[2] Siemens Manual Vertical Induction Motors EN, p. 9 · Alignment Procedure (Hollow Shaft)
Hollow shaft units require accurate alignment with respect to the unit shaft and the driven/drive equipment shaft. The pump shaft acts as a pendulum supported by the top coupling and unit bearing.
Align the unit as follows:
1. Clamp dial indicator to pump shaft, align with basebolt plane and set dial indicator to zero (Figure 2).
2. Remove top cover and rotate both unit and pump shafts.
3. Read dial indicator at 90 degree increments from starting point.
4. Acceptable alignment occurs when indicator readings do not exceed 0.0005 inches.
5. Shim flange faces if necessary (Figure 3).
When alignment and vibration of unit are within limits, engage drive. Run unit at minimum load and check for vibration - continue to increase load and checking vibration until full load is obtained.

The following checking procedure applies to a unit consisting of motor/generator, coupling, and a driven/drive component. Although applicable to most types of couplings, it is primarily intended for the rabbet-fit type. For other types, where the procedures differ, refer to the coupling manufacturer's Installation and Maintenance Instructions.
Work in one plane at a time and test for parallel or angular alignment with a dial indicator mounted as shown in Figure 1. Proceed as follows:
1. Set indicator dial to zero, at starting point.
2. Slowly turn both coupling halves a complete turn.
3. Observe dial reading at 90 degree increments from starting point.
4. Acceptable parallel alignment occurs when the total indicator readings do not exceed 0.002 inches.
5. Acceptable angular alignment occurs when the total indicator readings do not exceed 0.002 in./ft. radius to dial indicator.

[4] Nidec Motor Manual, p. 25 · Method 3 (refer to Figure 9)
This method uses a one inch thick steel disc, with center hole for shaft end bolt, and two threaded hydraulic jacks connected to a single pump. Apply load to the hydraulic jack until the dial indicator shows no movement on the end of the shaft. (See figure 7 for location of dial indicator.) Pressure from the hydraulic jack should be relieved until .005 to .008 end play is obtained. Lock the locknut with the lock washer.

results.question: What drying temperature does Siemens give for Class F insulation, and what must be done before reaching it?
results.expected_answer: 245°F (118°C); Class F and H units are first baked at 70% of the specified temperature for about six hours
results.rewritten_query: Siemens Class F motor insulation drying temperature and required steps before reaching the specified temperature.
results.answer:
## Siemens Class F drying temperature

The Siemens drying temperature for **Class F insulation is 245°F (118°C)**. Before reaching this temperature, bake the winding at **70% of the specified temperature for approximately six hours** to avoid steam forming inside the winding. [1]

| Insulation class | Drying temperature |
|---|---:|
| Class F | 245°F (118°C) [1] |

## Drying procedure and conditions

1. Apply heat slowly; the desired drying temperature should not be reached in less than six hours. [1]
2. For Class F insulation, hold the winding at 70% of the specified drying temperature for about six hours before raising it to 245°F (118°C). [1]
3. Measure insulation resistance before applying heat and every six to eight hours afterward. [1]
4. Use a warm-air oven, electric strip heaters, or circulating current through the coils as the heat source. [1]

For electric strip-heater drying, remove the bearing housings and rotor, direct a fan at the stator to remove moisture, attach temperature indicators to the winding, and follow the specified heating procedure. [2] Radiant heaters are not recommended because they may scorch some areas before remote parts reach the required temperature. [2]

results.question: When shimming between flanges on a Siemens vertical motor, how thick should the minor shims be and how far may shims penetrate?
results.expected_answer: Minor shims are one-half the thickness of the major shim; shims must not penetrate deeper than the bolt hole circle and not be wider than twice the penetration distance (Figure 3)
results.rewritten_query: For a Siemens vertical motor, what is the recommended thickness of minor shims placed between flanges, and what maximum distance may the shims penetrate between the flanges?
results.answer:
## Required shim dimensions

Minor shims should be **one-half the thickness of the major shim**:

$$t_{\text{minor}}=\frac{1}{2}t_{\text{major}}$$

[1]

For example, if the major shim is **0.050 in**, each minor shim should be **0.025 in** thick. [5]

![Figure 3](diagrams/a03aca4e-dbdc-4868-a843-4c240457390e/fig3_1.png)

Shims must **not penetrate deeper than the bolt-hole circle** and should be **no wider than twice their penetration distance**. [1]

## Installation and checks

1. Determine the major shim thickness and make the minor shims one-half as thick. [1]
2. Position the shims so their penetration does not extend past the bolt-hole circle and their width does not exceed twice the penetration distance. [1]
3. Tighten the flange mounting bolts, then check end play. [4]
4. Run the unit at minimum load and check vibration. [4]
5. If vibration is excessive, loosen the flange mounting bolts and shift the motor within the mounting-flange clearance; if this does not reduce vibration and the unit is coupled to a load, check shaft alignment and system reed frequency. [4]

results.rewritten_query: What regreasing interval, in operating hours, does the Siemens motor manual specify for the lower bearing?
results.answer:
## Answer

The provided context does not specify a Siemens-manual regreasing interval in operating hours for the lower bearing. No Siemens-specific lower-bearing interval appears in the supplied passages.

The available guidance states that:

- The applicable regreasing interval should be taken from the machine’s bearing plate, and bearings must be regreased at least once per year. [1]
- ABB’s standard interval basis is a bearing operating temperature of 70°C; the interval should be halved for each 15°C increase and may be doubled for each 15°C decrease. [1]
- Higher-speed frequency-converter operation or lower-speed operation under heavy load may require shorter intervals or a special lubricant. [3]
- During relubrication, the motor must be stopped and electrically isolated; the grease drain should be checked, compatible grease added, and the motor run for 15–30 minutes with the drain plug removed to purge excess grease. [2]

[1] ABB Manual for Induction Motors and Generators EN, p. 85 · 7.5.3.3 Re-greasing intervals
Rolling bearings of electrical machines need to be re-greased at regular intervals. The re-greasing interval is found on the bearing plate.
NOTE:
Regardless of the re-greasing interval, the bearings need to be re-greased at least once per year.
The re-greasing intervals are calculated for an operating temperature of 70°C (160°F). If the operating temperature is lower or higher than the assumed, the re-grease interval has to be altered accordingly. Higher operating temperature decreases the re-greasing interval.
NOTE:
An increase in the ambient temperature raises the temperature of the bearings correspondingly. The values for the re-greasing interval should be halved for every 15°C (30°F) increase in bearing temperature and may be once doubled for a 15°C (30°F) decrease in bearing temperature.

[2] Nidec Motor Manual, p. 29 · Lubrication Instructions
Question: How can motors in service be relubricated?
Answer Units are pre-lubricated at the factory and do not require initial lubrication. Relubricating interval depends upon speed, type of bearing and service. Refer to table in the Operating and Instruction Manual provided with motor for suggested re-greasing intervals and recommended greases. Operating conditions may dictate more frequent lubrication. Motor must be at rest and electrical controls should be locked open to prevent energizing while motor is being serviced (refer to section on Safety). If motor is being taken out of storage, refer to storage procedures.
To re-lubricate bearings, remove the drain plug. Inspect grease drain and remove any blockage with a mechanical probe taking care not to damage bearing. Under no circumstances should a mechanical probe be used while the motor is in operation. Add new grease at the grease inlet. New grease must be compatible with grease already in the motor (refer to Table 1 in Operating & Maintenance Manual for replenishment quantities). Run the motor for 15 to 30 minutes with the drain plug removed to allow purging of any excess grease. Shut off unit and replace the drain plug. Return motor to service.

[3] ABB Manual for Induction Motors and Generators EN, p. 85 · Re-greasing intervals for frequency converter drives
Higher speed operation, e.g. in frequency converter applications, or lower speed with heavy load will require shorter lubrication intervals or a special lubricant. Consult ABB Motors and Generators Service in such cases.
NOTE:
The constructional maximum speed of the machine must not be exceeded. The suitability of the bearings for high-speed operation must be checked.

[4] ABB Manual for Induction Motors and Generators EN, p. 84 · 7.5.2.5 Oil change schedule for mineral oils
For self-lubricated bearings cleaning intervals with oil changes of approximately 8000 operating hours are recommended and approx. 20000 operating hours for bearings with oil circulation systems.
Shorter oil change intervals may be necessary in case of frequent start-ups, high oil temperatures or excessively high contamination due to external influences.
The correct oil change interval can be found on the bearing plate and dimensional drawing, see Chapter 2.1.2 Bearing plate.
Following chapter for bearing type: Rolling bearing

[5] ABB Manual for Induction Motors and Generators EN, p. 66 · Figure 32 Example of lubrication channel through bearing arrangement of horizontal machine
NOTE:
NOTE:
Start-up greasing may take several grease portions (3-10 times amount mentioned at the lubrication plate).
The re-lubrication interval will never be longer than 12 months.
The type of original grease used is found on the bearing plate on the machine. Acceptable types of grease can be found in Chapter 7.5.3 Rolling bearings.
NOTE:
Do not mix greases! There must be only one type of grease inside the bearing - not mixture of two or more greases.
The temperature of the bearings will initially increase because of the excess grease. After few hours, the excess grease will be discharged through the lubrication valve and the temperature of the bearing will return to normal running temperature.

## Tightening torque

**Use 390 Nm for an M20, strength class 8.8 screw with a standard thread.** [1]

| Thread | Strength class | Tightening torque |
|---|---:|---:|
| M20 standard thread | 8.8 | 390 Nm [1] |

1. Verify that the fastener is **M20**, **strength class 8.8**, and has a **standard thread**. [1]
2. Confirm whether the screw has the **FLZN/480H** surface treatment; if so, use **335 Nm** rather than 390 Nm. [1]
3. If the fastener uses a fine thread or another special configuration, do not apply the standard-thread value without the applicable specific instruction. [1]

results.answer:
## Tightening torque

The tightening torque is **117 Nm** for an **M12, strength class 10.9 screw with a standard metric thread**. [1]

| Screw | Strength class | Tightening torque |
|---|---:|---:|
| M12, standard thread | 10.9 | 117 Nm [1] |

## Conditions and procedure

1. Confirm that the screw is an **M12 standard-thread fastener** and is marked or specified as **strength class 10.9**. [1]
2. Apply **117 Nm** using a calibrated torque wrench. [1]
3. Do not use this value without further confirmation if the screw has a **fine thread**; the manual states that fine-thread screws require a specific tightening instruction. [1]
4. Do not substitute the high-temperature-screw values unless the fastener is identified as a high-temperature screw, because those screws have separate tightening values and markings. [5]

The provided context does not identify the exact KD27V12 fastening location, so it does not establish whether the screw is a fine-thread or high-temperature application.

Winding thermostats are snap action, bi-metallic, temperature actuated switches. Their purpose is to activate a warning device, or simply shut down the motor upon excessive winding temperatures, when wired into the motor control circuit.
Thermostats are made either with contacts that are normally closed (open at high temperatures) or contacts that are normally open (closed at high temperatures). The thermostat temperature switch point is pre-calibrated by the manufacturer and is not adjustable. Reset is automatic after a decrease in temperature. Thermostats are normally installed in the connection end turns of the motor winding. Standard procedure is to wire three thermostats together in a set, with one thermostat embedded in each phase of the winding. Open thermostats are normally wired in parallel, while closed thermostats are wired in series. Refer to the figure below for further explanation.

results.question: If the fuel sulfur content is between 0.5% and 1%, how does the Kohler engine oil change interval change?
results.expected_answer: Oil change factor 1/2 — the interval is halved; limited to engine oil categories 2 and 3
results.rewritten_query: Kohler engine oil change interval when fuel sulfur content is between 0.5% and 1%: required interval adjustment.
results.answer:
## Effect on the oil-change interval

For fuel sulfur content **greater than 0.5% and up to 1%**, the oil-change factor is **1/2**, so the interval is **reduced by half** for engine oil categories **2 and 3**. [1]

| Fuel sulfur content | Oil-change factor | Result |
|---|---:|---|
| \(0.5\% < \text{sulfur} \leq 1\%\) — limited to engine oil categories 2 and 3 | \(1/2\) | Oil-change interval is reduced by half [1] |

The calculation is:

$$
\text{Change interval}
=
\text{Basic change interval}
\times
\text{Oil-category factor}
\times
\frac{1}{2}
$$

[1]

## Procedure

1. Determine the applicable basic interval from the maintenance table for the genset application and engine injection calibration. [1]
2. Confirm that the engine oil is category 2 or 3, because this sulfur range is limited to those categories. [1]
3. Apply the sulfur factor of \(1/2\), reducing the resulting oil-change interval by half. [1]
4. If difficult operating conditions apply—such as frequent cold starts, dust, high humidity, or long downtimes—validate the interval through engine oil analysis. [1][2]

results.expected_answer: 6 months (outdoors under a film cover up to one month); for over 6 and up to 24 months contact Field Service
results.rewritten_query: Kohler engine conservation protection: duration of protection during normal dry storage and requirements for storage periods longer than the specified duration.
results.answer:
## Conservation period

In a **dry, ventilated storage location**, the Kohler engine’s conservation protection lasts **6 months** from the date it is ready for delivery. [1]

For storage **longer than 6 months**, the provided context does not specify an approved extension or re-conservation procedure; it states that unfavorable storage conditions can shorten the protection period. [1]

## Conditions and limits

- With a **waterproof film cover**, loosely fitted to allow air circulation and prevent condensation, the engine may be stored outdoors for **up to 1 month**. [1]
- Longer outdoor exposure, or storage in damp and unventilated conditions, is expected to shorten the conservation-protection period. [1]
- Storage conditions are the responsibility of the system manufacturer, and ISO 6749-1984 should be observed for transport and storage. [5]
- Only preservatives approved by Kohler Co. should be used. [5]

## Recommended procedure

1. Store the engine in a dry, ventilated location and treat the conservation protection as valid for up to 6 months. [1]
2. If outdoor storage is unavoidable, use a waterproof cover fitted loosely enough for air circulation, and limit outdoor storage to 1 month. [1]
3. For storage beyond the stated limits, obtain instructions from Kohler customer service because the context does not define the required preservation renewal or inspection procedure. [5]

results.question: What fuel pipe diameter does EMSA recommend for an 800–1500 kVA standby generator, and what are the pipe length and height limits?
results.expected_answer: 1 1/2 inch; maximum 6 m length, 0.9 m vertical height, 6 pipe fittings
results.rewritten_query: EMSA recommended fuel pipe diameter, maximum pipe length, and maximum height difference for an 800–1500 kVA standby diesel generator fuel system.
results.answer:
## Recommended fuel pipe sizing

For an **800–1500 kVA standby generator**, EMSA recommends a **1 1/2-inch fuel pipe**, with a maximum pipe length of **6 m** and a maximum vertical height of **0.9 m**. The maximum number of pipe fittings is **6**. [1]

| Standby generator power | Recommended pipe diameter | Maximum pipe length | Maximum vertical height | Maximum fittings | Source |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| 800–1500 kVA | 1 1/2 in | 6 m | 0.9 m | 6 | [1] |

## Installation checks

1. Apply positive static fuel pressure at the fuel-pump intake for fuel-tank applications installed with the standby generator assembly. [1]
2. Use check valves if the fuel tank is **2 m above the centre of the crankshaft**. [1]
3. Keep the maximum fuel level no more than **2 m above the centre of the crankshaft**. [1]
4. Keep the minimum fuel level **15 cm above the fuel injection pump**; below this level, proper fuel-pump intake pressure cannot be provided. [1]
5. Do not exceed the stated pipe length, vertical-height, or fitting limits, because these are EMSA’s listed maximum recommendations for this generator-power range. [1]

results.question: When adding electrolyte to an EMSA maintenance-type battery for the first time, what density and level are required, and how long is the minimum charge?
results.expected_answer: Specific density 1.280 at 20°C, filled to 15 mm above the plates (electrolyte above 10°C); minimum charging period 6 hours
results.rewritten_query: EMSA maintenance-type battery: during initial electrolyte filling, what electrolyte density and level are required, and what is the minimum charging time?
results.answer:
## Required values

- **Electrolyte density:** **1.270–1.280 specific density**, corresponding to a fully charged battery. [2]
- **Electrolyte level:** Add distilled water until the electrolyte is **10 mm above the plates**. [1]
- **Minimum charge/observation period:** Check the electrolyte level every **1 hour**; the battery is considered charged if **no change is observed after 1 hour**. [1]

## Procedure

1. Add electrolyte to the maintenance-type battery for the first time. [1]
2. Check the electrolyte level at **1-hour intervals**. [1]
3. Add distilled water as necessary to maintain the electrolyte **10 mm above the plates**. [1]
4. Confirm the specific density is **1.270–1.280** for a fully charged condition. [2]
5. Treat the battery as charged when no electrolyte-level change is observed after **1 hour**. [1]

The provided context does not specify a longer charging duration beyond this one-hour criterion.

This maintenance instruction must be fully implemented periodically to maintain radiator efficiency and warranty support coverage. If any maintenance steps are missed, any warranty issues may not be covered by EMSA.
- The radiator must be filled slowly and carefully, leaving no air space inside.
- Balance and order must be ensured by checking the physical condition of the fan blades.
- The tension of the belts connecting the engine and radiator ulleys must also be checked for looseness, cracks, damage or defects. After the checks, loose belts must be tightened and damaged belts should be replaced.

- In order not to make any adjustments at the bottom of the radiator and to ensure that the coolant remains homogeneous, he engine must be started at predetermined intervals (by the engine manufacturer) and the radiator's coolant must be circulated periodically.
- No foreign substance or any substance other than the coolant mixture (antifreeze, water, some protective chemicals…) must be placed or dripped into the radiator.
- Radiators that have not been used for 6 months or more must be washed and cleaned inside before use.
- Necessary measures must be taken against vibration, especially between the radiator and chassis connection.
- Lifting lugs must be used as handles when lifting the radiator.
- The radiator cap must be replaced once a year.
- While carrying the radiator, the user should be very careful to avoid damage to the radiator's connection points (welding, bolts, etc.).

The connections of the main power cables must be designed to withstand demanding operation conditions where the insulators can be subjected to dirt, humidity and surge voltages. In order to ensure lasting and trouble-free running, it is therefore important that the length of the insulation and creepage distances are sufficient. The minimum insulation and creepage distances should be equal or exceed demands set by:
- Local requirements
- Standards
- Classification rules
- Hazardous area classification.
The insulation and creepage distances apply both for insulation distances between two different phases, and for insulation distances between one phase and earth. The air insulation distance is the shortest distance through air between two points with different electrical potential (voltage). The surface creepage distance is the shortest distance along surfaces next to each other between two points with different electrical potential (voltage).

[3] Siemens Manual Vertical Induction Motors EN, p. 20 · Maintenance
For best results, grease should be compounded of a polyurea type and a good grade of petroleum oil and stabilized against oxidation.
The frequency of relubricating bearings and the amount added each time depends on two factors - speed and service.
All grease lube bearing motors will have affixed a plate with lubricating instructions. The instructions on this plate should be followed to achieve optimum bearing life and to avoid consequential damage to rotating parts.
Relubricate with the type of grease specified on the lubrication plate mounted on the motor, or compatible grease. Mixing of non-compatible greases can cause bearing failure.
Relubricate bearings with the proper grade of grease as follows:
1. Stop the motor and lock out the switch.
2. Thoroughly clean the grease inlet fitting or plug. If the motor has a plug, remove plug and clean the inlet.
3. Remove the drain plug (and overflow plug, if so equipped) and clean out any hardened grease.
4. Slowly pump the correct amount of grease into the grease inlet, per the lubrication plate mounted on the motor. Replace inlet plug (and overflow plug, if so equipped).
5. Start motor and allow to run at least one (1) hour to expel any excess grease from the drain opening before re-installing the drain plug.
6. Stop the motor and lock out the switch.
7. Re-install the drain plug.
8. Put the motor back in operation.

[4] Siemens Manual Vertical Induction Motors EN, p. 19 · Bearing Lubricants - Grease
Prior to shipment, bearings are lubricated with the proper amount and grade of grease to provide satisfactory service under normal operation and conditions. See the lubrication plate mounted on the motor for regreasing intervals and recommended type of grease. It is good practice, however, to check bearings of newly installed machines for proper lubrication.

[5] ABB Manual for Induction Motors and Generators EN, p. 21 · Following bullet for bearing type: Rolling bearing
- Ball and roller bearings are greased with lubricant indicated on the bearing plate, which is attached to the machine frame, see Chapter 2.1.2 Bearing plate.

results.question: Which grease is the ABB example rolling-bearing plate (Figure 4) delivered with, and how often must the waste grease box be emptied?
results.expected_answer: ESSO UNIREX N2; empty the waste grease box every 6th relubrication
results.rewritten_query: What type of grease is specified for the ABB example rolling-bearing plate shown in Figure 4, and what is the required interval for emptying the waste-grease box?
results.answer:
## Direct answer

The ABB example rolling-bearing plate was delivered from the factory with **ESSO UNIREX N2** grease, and the **waste grease box must be emptied after every sixth relubrication**. [1]

![Figure 4 Bearing plate for grease lubricated rolling bearings](diagrams/41ec3469-76ef-43af-af26-ddc71f09336b/fig4_1.png)

## Maintenance instruction

1. Count each relubrication operation. [1]
2. Empty the waste grease box after the **6th relubrication**. [1]
